description: Evaluate polynomial expressions and integer powers of complex numbers, including sums of powers of i using the period-4 cycle.

source.description: Cambodian BAC II grade-12 math textbook, Chapter 1 (complex numbers, algebraic form) — exercises only
source.extracted_by: manual OCR/transcription from scanned textbook (Claude Code), 2026-08-25

exercises.technique: Substitute z into the polynomial and expand using i^2=-1.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Given } u=3+2i \text{ and } v=2-i. \text{ Compute } z = u^2-uv+v^2.
exercises.technique: Expand each term using i^2=-1 and combine real/imaginary parts.
Substitute a, simplify numerator, then divide by multiplying by the conjugate of the denominator.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Given } z=2+3i. \text{ Compute } z^2,\ z^3 \text{ and } z^4.
exercises.technique: Binomial expansion (a+bi)^n using i^2=-1, i^3=-i, i^4=1.
Use the periodicity of powers of i (period 4: i^{4n}=1, i^{4n+1}=i, i^{4n+2}=-1, i^{4n+3}=-i) to group and sum the terms.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Given the complex numbers } a=2+i,\ b=1-3i,\ c=-3+2i. \text{ (a) Write } z=a^3+b^3+c^3 \text{ and } w=abc \text{ in algebraic form.}
exercises.technique: Compute each cube via binomial expansion, sum them for z, and multiply the three numbers directly for w.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Given } z=a^3+b^3+c^3 \text{ and } w=abc \text{ from the previous part (}a=2+i,\ b=1-3i,\ c=-3+2i\text{). (b) Show that } \frac{z}{w} \text{ is a real number.}
exercises.technique: Compute the quotient z/w (e.g. by multiplying by the conjugate of w) and verify its imaginary part is zero.
